what: Arrow Electronics distributes electronic components. It buys chips, connectors and passive parts from manufacturers and sells them to the companies that build electronic products, and it also resells enterprise computing.
customers: Electronics manufacturers of every size, and the resellers who serve corporate IT buyers.
money: servers, storage and software sold through resellers
moat: Relationships with hundreds of component makers and tens of thousands of customers, plus the inventory and engineering support that smaller manufacturers cannot do without.
risks: A 1.8% net margin: distribution lives on volume
Revenue fell from $37.1B to $27.9B in the component downturn before recovering
opportunities: 9.3 times earnings with $669M of free cash flow
Revenue recovered to $30.9B last year and is $38.9B over the last twelve months
Analysts see about 18% upside, and component inventories across the industry have largely normalised
watch: Component segment sales growth and the book-to-bill ratio.
